SMTO-DB-0005 — SMTO needs your approval before it changes your database

GUID: 759e9001-9185-4614-ad35-0d105c69f48f
Slug: database-mutation-authorization-required
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • SMTO wanted to run a database command that changes data or isn't a plain read, and it didn't have your approval to do that. Nothing in your database was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you only wanted to look at data, tell SMTO in the conversation to use a query that only reads and changes nothing. Read-only questions don't need approval, so SMTO can answer them right away.
  2. If you want the change, ask SMTO to describe exactly what it will change. When an Approval needed card appears, read it, then select Approve once or Deny / stop task. SMTO only changes your database after you approve that exact change.
  3. If other people also edit this database, ask SMTO to look at the current data again before you approve. Approving a change built on old data could overwrite someone else's newer work.

What success looks like

  • SMTO either answers with read-only results, or reports that the change you approved finished.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change permission settings to allow every database change just to avoid the approval step.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SQL classification marked the statement as a mutation (or rejected a non-SELECT/CTE form), and execution was refused because no privilege_allowed authorization was present for it.

What this means

  • SQL safety classification rejects unsupported statement forms, or a mutation requiring confirmation reaches execution without privilege_allowed authorization. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • SQL safety classification rejects unsupported statement forms, or a mutation requiring confirmation reaches execution without privilege_allowed authorization.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safety_classification.reason to distinguish unsupported_statement from confirmation_required before requesting approval.

How to fix it

  • Read-only work must be a single SELECT or WITH ... SELECT statement. Statements containing INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, CREATE, ALTER, COPY, MERGE, transactions or other commands require the normal approval path, which sets privilege_allowed for that exact action. Re-inspect the current target rows or objects before approving, and never reuse an approval or identifier from before another actor changed the data.
  • Use a supported SQL statement; obtain the normal exact-target authorization when a supported mutation requires it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The statement is supported and any exact mutation authorization is present before dispatch.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
